method: Pearson correlation between a growing-season (April–September) climatic water-deficit proxy, 1 − P/ET0 from NASA POWER, and the standardised anomaly of growing-season mean MODIS NDVI at the field centre pixel, one value per year.
caveats: Fixture only: the stress series is a simple climatic proxy, not the Travertine engine's crop water-balance model.
NDVI comes from a single 250 m pixel without cloud or quality filtering; it may mix several fields and land uses.
Irrigation is not represented: irrigated fields can stay green in dry years, which weakens the relationship.
24 years is a small sample; the correlation is uncertain and shows association, not causation.

provenance.dataset: NASA POWER monthly point data (MERRA-2 and GEWEX SRB derived), AG community
provenance.provider: NASA Langley Research Center, POWER Project
provenance.note: Parameters PRECTOTCORR_SUM, T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, GWETROOT. Annual ET0 is computed by summing monthly Hargreaves–Samani estimates (FAO-56 eq. 52) from POWER temperatures and FAO-56 extraterrestrial radiation; Hargreaves can overestimate ET0 in humid or windy conditions.

provenance.dataset: MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices 16-Day L3 Global 250 m (MOD13Q1 v061)
provenance.provider: NASA LP DAAC, accessed via ORNL DAAC MODIS Web Service
provenance.note: Single pixel at the field centre. Growing-season mean of the ten composites starting day-of-year 97 to 241. Quality flags not yet applied.
